A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SAME and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables and appendices. The complete 17-page v1 and 25-page v2 support reliable comparison despite appendix reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original CoIN evaluations, component ablations, router/expert-drift diagnostics, efficiency measurements and qualitative analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds TriGap, UCIT, robustness, design-choice and out-of-distribution evaluations.

M1.justification: The spectral-aware routing, curvature-aware scaling and adaptive freezing procedures remain unchanged, as do Algorithms 1–2. The revised experimental setup and newly disclosed decomposition implementation do not establish a change to the proposed method.

E1.justification: Beyond CoIN, v2 evaluates UCIT, the new ten-task TriGap benchmark and cross-benchmark transfer to MMMU. Coverage expands to captioning, medical and chemical questions, documents/charts, traffic scenes, aerial disaster imagery and additional reasoning tasks.

E2.justification: The seven CoIN comparators are retained. New comparisons actually evaluate Zero-shot, FT-LoRA, Replay-LoRA and CL-MoE on TriGap/UCIT; Table 9 additionally evaluates GPM-style hard-projection and VPT-CPG-style constant-scaling substitutions.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 changes the reported setup from LoRA in all linear layers with a projector learning rate to FFN-only LoRA training. This does not establish that retained experiments were rerun. New protocols include UCIT-based hyperparameter selection, alternative CoIN task orders, fixed-expert/representation controls and quantitative forgetting evaluation.

E4.justification: Appendices F–L add hyperparameter sensitivity, task-order robustness, scaling/freezing design comparisons, freezing-related routing entropy, controlled router-drift causality, quantitative forgetting, MMMU generalization and compression/efficiency analyses. These substantially extend the retained component ablations and diagnostic plots.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed or repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, standard deviations or significance tests. The additional results continue to use point estimates.

E6.justification: The original CoIN comparison and component-ablation values remain unchanged, including SAME's 66.82 average. v2 adds TriGap and UCIT averages of 46.53 and 67.12, MMMU results of 36.35 for SAME versus 34.83 for MoELoRA, and numerous analysis results. These are additional evaluations, not same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: The main projection argument and Riemannian update remain. However, v2 Appendix D introduces a Neural Feature Matrix–AGOP proportionality with exponent 1/2 and replaces the detailed Jacobian derivation. Appendix C removes explicit LoRA-factor approximation qualifications and changes approximate constraint saturation to equality.

C1.justification: The abstract now explicitly claims introducing a benchmark for long-sequence MCIT, developed as TriGap in Section 5.1. This adds an independent benchmark contribution to v1's method contribution; the two-drift diagnosis, three method components and general performance claims remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive explanations of hyperparameter sensitivity, subtraction versus ratio scoring, anisotropic scaling versus projection, structured expert specialization, isolated router-induced forgetting and transferable capabilities. Appendix L also links routing stability to sparse inference. The original limitations concerning ambiguous task boundaries and varying formats remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds a Prism code pointer and infrastructure reference, selected hyperparameters, selection using 20% of UCIT training data, per-task TriGap sample counts, and randomized top-64 decomposition/storage details. It also explicitly identifies the retained CoIN baseline scores as adopted from original publications.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands positioning through TriGap's claimed gaps relative to CoIN/UCIT and explicit distinctions from GPM-style projection and VPT-CPG-style scaling. It adds dataset, infrastructure and methodological references and expands comparator descriptions; the orthogonal-subspace-learning and SmoLoRA references are removed.

P1.justification: Most introduction, method and conclusion prose and the main section sequence remain intact. Rewriting is concentrated in benchmark discussion and mathematical appendices. Pseudocode moves from Appendix E to A, other appendices are reorganized, and affiliations, publication information and acknowledgments are updated.

P2.justification: v2 adds benchmark tables, an extensive appendix table suite and a full-page TriGap example figure. Figure 2 gains boxed visual groupings, while retained tables and plots are relocated. The original layer-wise utilization plot is preserved as Figure 10 rather than newly added.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens validation beyond CoIN through additional domains, controlled drift experiments, robustness tests and design comparisons. Previously missing hyperparameters and code-access information also improve reproducibility. These gains outweigh localized regressions: Table 12 has inconsistent forgetting signs and a MoELoRA average incompatible with its listed values, while the theoretical appendices make LoRA-factor approximation qualifications less explicit.
